adversarialFindings.title: An existing G-75 guard is a whole-file substring test and it fired on 30b's own .finding value. It fired twice.
adversarialFindings.detail: src/ui.test.mjs:179 asserts /align-items: start/.test(shell) === false. It is scoped to nothing: it reads the entire stylesheet as one string. 30b's .finding declares align-items:start, so the verbatim port failed the suite at 184/185 on the first run.
adversarialFindings.secondFiring: The first fix wrote a comment explaining the swap, and the comment quoted the literal string align-items: start, so the guard fired again on prose. That is a real property of a substring guard and worth recording: it cannot tell a declaration from a sentence about a declaration. The comment was reworded rather than the guard touched.
adversarialFindings.resolution: Shipped align-items: flex-start on .finding. On a grid container flex-start is defined to behave as start (CSS Box Alignment level 3 treats the flex-relative keywords as start/end outside flex layout), so rendering is unchanged. .cite.model already carries flex-start from 30b itself, so the file is now internally consistent on the keyword.
adversarialFindings.whyNotFixTheGuard: The guard is over-broad by construction, but it is a G-75 layout invariant this row was not scoped to touch, and weakening a live guard to admit a cosmetically-equivalent value is the wrong trade. A behaviourally-identical keyword costs nothing. Recorded so the planner can decide whether to scope the guard to .shell-regions in its own row.
adversarialFindings.backlogCandidate: scope ui.test.mjs:179 to the selectors G-75 actually governs, rather than the whole file

adversarialFindings.title: The predicted denominator was 138 and the measured one is 139. Reconciled, not rounded off.
adversarialFindings.detail: The investigation predicted 109 + 29 = 138 for four families. Measured after the port: 139, i.e. 30 tokens added, not 29.
adversarialFindings.reconciliation: The gap is entirely in the fourth family and the investigation's own text flagged it as a conditional: 'finding, crit, fid, fbody, ftitle, fmeta, fact, basisline, conf, meter; the meter fill f makes 11 if .f is not already counted'. The CP1 collision check measured .f at zero occurrences in both stylesheets, so it is not already counted and the family is 11 tokens, not 10. The three-family figure of 19 was exact: cite 4, mx 11, atomchip 4. 19 + 11 = 30. The 138 headline took the low branch of its own stated conditional.
adversarialFindings.note: The WDLL already says 138 is an estimate and not the acceptance value, and that the recount is the only authority. This is that recount, taken in the product repo; the kit-side pin is WDLL item 4 and is a different lane's arithmetic on the same rule.

adversarialFindings.title: The class gate runs one-directional, so CSS with no markup cannot trip it, and that is by design.
adversarialFindings.detail: ui.test.mjs's 'composes existing kit classes and declares no new one' builds a defined set from shell + kit and asserts used minus defined is empty. Adding definitions with no users grows the permissive side only. Verified by the suite passing at 185. The reverse direction - a defined class nobody uses - is not gated in this repo and this PR ships 30 of them deliberately, because the screens that use them are WDLL item 9.
adversarialFindings.consequence: Between this merge and item 9 the product carries 30 classes with rules and no markup. That is the intended intermediate state, but it is the state in which a coverage claim of the form 'every shipped class is used' would be false. Recorded so nobody reads the gate's silence as a claim.
